objective: Measure the validation-quality and activation-frequency tradeoff as the train-only input-reconstruction loss is weakened over a powers-of-four coefficient sweep.
comparison_policy: Reuse the already-complete beta=0 fuzzy parent and beta=1 reconstruction endpoints. Launch only beta=1/4, 1/16, and 1/64 at the same three paired seeds. Do not select or stop cells from intermediate loss or sparsity observations.
gradient_interpretation: For shared encoder parameters, beta scales the reconstruction contribution in grad(cross_entropy + beta * reconstruction_nmse). Parameters private to W_rec receive only the scaled reconstruction gradient, whose physical Adam update need not shrink proportionally because of adaptive normalization; W_rec is discarded at deployment.

common.sparsity_capture_steps: step 1, every 100 steps, and exact final step

systems_gate.reason: The recipe implementation, tensor shapes, topology, data, and observer already passed two systems gates and six full endpoints. This study changes only a finite scalar loss coefficient.

primary: canonical validation loss by paired seed
validation-loss delta versus beta=0 and beta=1
activation_frequency: final sampled-batch dead-feature fraction by layer
dead-feature fraction across the final ten aligned captures
per-layer activation-frequency Gini and high-frequency tail
positive-group fraction and within-group winner entropy
reconstruction: reconstruction NMSE by layer and step

launch_policy: Launch only the nine missing lower-beta endpoints. Use a Latin-square arm order across seeds so each coefficient appears once in each queue position. Every admitted cell runs the complete 4656-step schedule.
stopping_rule: Any systems or artifact-validation failure stops the sequential queue for inspection. Never retry automatically after an incomplete attempt.
evidence_boundary: This is a paired three-seed dose-response study at 125M on one v4-32 topology. It can locate a 125M quality-utilization frontier but cannot establish coefficient transfer across model scale.
